title: fix(objectql): a tree field's deleteBehavior takes effect on a parent delete
body:
Fixes #22957
Clause-②: no

The engine's referential delete walk now follows `tree` fields. The `deleteBehavior` the spec declares on a `tree` (materialized as `set_null` when the author writes none) takes effect on a by-id delete of the parent. This follows triage's ruling (comment 6119365636): the runtime honours the declared behaviour, and the spec's materialization stays as it is.

## What changed

- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`: one family predicate, `statesDeleteSemantics` over `DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES` (`master_detail`, `lookup`, `tree`), replaces the `master_detail` / `lookup` literal at both readers of the delete walk that tested the family. A `tree` resolves like a `lookup`: an authored value is used as written, and an absent one resolves to `set_null`.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-tree.test.ts`: 18 pins, listed below.
- `.changeset/22957-tree-delete-behavior.md`: `patch` for `@objectstack/objectql`.

## Readers of the walk (read on `origin/main` `9f4b652e3a`)

| reader | family test before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `cascadeRelationBehavior` | `master_detail` / `lookup` literal | the predicate |
| `collectCascadeDeleteSet` (phase 1) | reads `cascadeRelationBehavior` | code unchanged, widened through it |
| `walkReferencingRelations` (phase 2, the dependents walk) | reads `cascadeRelationBehavior` | code unchanged, widened through it |
| `planCascadeAtomicity` and its `referenceCarrierOf` probe | `master_detail` / `lookup` literal | the predicate, so a subtree cascade is one unit of work |
| the #9625 resolved-behaviour reads: the `master_detail` coercion to `cascade`, the `master_detail` + `set_null` warning, and the required `set_null` escalation to `restrict` | read the resolved behaviour | unchanged. A `tree` takes the `lookup` branch, so a required tree's `set_null` escalates like a required lookup's (pinned) |
| the `referenceCarrierOf` call in `buildSummaryIndex` | `master_detail` / `lookup` literal | **left as is.** It resolves a roll-up summary's foreign key and is not part of the delete walk |

## Measured before and after

### `os verify --app examples/app-showcase/objectstack.config.ts --delete-behaviors --json`

Before: `9f4b652e3a`. After: objectql built from `2030d882ac`. `engine.ts` is byte-identical from there through this head, `85abb2ed96`.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| exit | 1 | 0 |
| `hardFailures` | 1 | 0 |
| `showcase_field_zoo.f_tree` (declared `set_null`) | contradicted. REST answered 200 and the system door succeeded, and both left the holder on the deleted id | proven. Both doors cleared it (`holderValue: null`) |
| the other 23 rows | 8 proven, 1 inconclusive (`showcase_invoice.contact`, refused by an app validation rule), 11 excluded, 3 not-derivable | identical, row by row |

### Real driver: ObjectQL + `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), a scratch probe (not committed)

| case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tree, `set_null` materialized by `FieldSchema.parse` | child keeps the deleted id | child's parent is `null` |
| tree registered raw, no key | child keeps the deleted id | child's parent is `null` |
| tree `cascade`: delete `a` from root, a, b, c (a chain) plus a2 and an unrelated pair | only `a` deleted | `a`, `b`, `c` deleted; root, a2 and the pair kept |
| tree `restrict` | parent deleted, child left dangling | `DELETE_RESTRICTED` 409 naming the tree's own object; both rows kept; the leaf then deletes |
| tree `cascade`, a 15-level chain | 1 of 15 deleted | 15 of 15 deleted |
| tree `cascade`, a corrupt cycle (root's parent is its grandchild) and a row that is its own parent | only the deleted row went | terminates (7 ms); every row of the cycle deleted once |
| tree registered raw with `multiple: true` | child keeps the deleted id | child's parent is `null` (read single-valued) |
| tree `cascade` with a `beforeDelete` veto on a deep node | root deleted, children kept (nothing walked) | refused 409; all four rows kept (rolled back) |
| CONTROL: `lookup` default `set_null`, `lookup` `cascade`, `master_detail` default | cleared / deleted / deleted | identical |
| CONTROL: `lookup` and `master_detail` `restrict` | both `DELETE_RESTRICTED` 409 | identical |

### The four questions the dispatch asked

- **`multiple: true`.** `FieldSchema` refuses `multiple: true` on a `tree` at parse: it is declarable only on select, lookup, user, file and image. `lookup` has a multi-valued path (the `$contains` probe and member removal). A `tree` cannot reach that path through the contract. The walk's multi-value arbiter `declaredMultiValued` asks the spec's `isMultiValueField`, which reads a raw-registered multi `tree` as single-valued, as every other engine site does. Nothing new was added for it.
- **The default.** The spec's parse puts `set_null` on a bare `tree`, and the test pins that as its premise. The engine reads the field raw, and an absent key also resolves to `set_null`. Both are pinned.
- **Depth and cycles.** `MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH` (10) bounds only `planCascadeAtomicity`'s schema walk. `cascadeDeleteRelations` has a `depth` parameter, but the nested deletes never advance it (the one call site passes the default), so the cascade over rows is bounded by its set. `collectCascadeDeleteSet` expands each record once, and the deleting walk skips a record it has already entered. Pinned: a 15-level chain is deleted whole, and a corrupt cycle and a self-parent both terminate.
- **Atomicity.** An object whose only relation is its own hierarchy used to plan `'none'` and opened no transaction. It now plans `'atomic'`, so a refusal deep in a subtree rolls back the nodes deleted before it.

## Pins (`engine-cascade-delete-tree.test.ts`, in-file driver with snapshot rollback)

- set_null: the parse premise; then materialized, authored, and absent: the child's parent is cleared, the child is kept, and a bystander is untouched (3 cases).
- cascade: a subtree with a single commit; 15 levels deleted whole; a corrupt cycle terminates; a self-parent terminates; a deep veto rolls everything back.
- restrict: the parent delete is refused with `code` + `status` + `dependentObject`, and both rows are kept; a leaf deletes.
- required: a required tree's `set_null` escalates to `DELETE_RESTRICTED`.
- multiple: the parse refuses `multiple: true` on a tree; a raw registration is read single-valued.
- CONTROLS: lookup default and cascade plus the master_detail default; lookup and master_detail `restrict` (2 cases); an object nothing references opens no transaction.

## Ablation (from the committed head `5ce34e0670`, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`)

Each leg's anchor hit 1 to 0 and the blob changed. After each leg the restore read blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` was empty.

- **Leg A**: `tree` dropped from `DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES` gave 11 failed and 7 passed. Red: all 11 tree-behaviour pins. Green: the 2 parse premises, the restrict leaf delete, and the 4 CONTROL tests.
- **Leg B**: only `planCascadeAtomicity`'s reader put back to the old literal gave 2 failed and 16 passed: the subtree's single-commit assertion and the deep-veto rollback. So the atomicity widening is pinned on its own.

## Tests

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/engine-cascade-delete-tree.test.ts`: 18 passed, at `5ce34e0670`.
- The full package suite (`vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`) ran at `2030d882ac` plus the then-uncommitted required pin: 406 files and 7953 tests passed, 1 failed. The failure was the required pin as first written: its fixture referenced a row that did not exist, and the engine's write-time reference check refused it. The fixture was corrected and passes in the single-file run above.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck`: exit 0, covering `tsc` and `check:test-typecheck`. The new file is in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (`--listFiles` count 1).
- `@objectstack/objectql`'s public surface is unchanged (no export, no type), so no importing package owes a test.

## Gates

`dispatch-gates --commands` on this head `85abb2ed96` derives 68 commands: the dispatched 57 plus 11 that the changeset brings in. All 68 exit 0. The `--ran` reconciliation reads 68 derived, 68 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, and that zero is derived from the recorded exit codes. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first answered PREREQUISITE NOT MET because 8 packages outside this diff had no `dist/`. They were built (all turbo cache hits), and the gate re-ran with exit 0.

## Deviations

- The pins use an in-file driver with snapshot rollback, the same shape as the five sibling `engine-cascade-delete-*` suites, not a real driver. `packages/objectql` lists no driver package among its dependencies, and adding one (to `package.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` and the test-source-alias ledger) is outside the claim's file surface. The real-driver evidence is the showcase verify (sqlite-wasm, through REST and the system door) and the scratch `SqlDriver` probe above.
- `origin/main` gained two docs-only commits (ADR text and anchor JSON) after the base. They were merged into this branch as `85abb2ed96`; no package changed.

## Acceptance notes

- A `tree` that omits `reference` is still not walked. `ObjectSchema` accepts it as a self-reference (the `refuseForeignTreeReference` rule: the reference stays optional), and the parse materializes `set_null` on it. But `referenceCarrierOf` reads no carrier, and `referenceTargetOf` calls a referenceless `tree` targetless. Measured on this head through REST: `DELETE` answered 200 and the child kept the deleted id. Repairing it is a spec decision: which of the two readings is the contract, and whether a referenceless tree's target should resolve to its owning object. That is not a consumer-side fallback to add here. Reported to the seat.
- Two comments in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` (the `deleteBehavior` TSDoc and the `.overwrite` block) still say that the engine reads the key only behind a `master_detail` / `lookup` guard. That now includes `tree`. These are comments only. Carrier: none. Noted, not filed.
- An authored `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field still parses and is still not walked. That is the spec's existing line for `user`, and this PR leaves it untouched.
